source.title_on_document: Exploring Language Patterns of Prompts in Text-to-Image Generation and Their Impact on Visual Diversity

supplement.where: Appendices A to E at the end of the same PDF (pp. 14-29)
supplement.holds: User-category counts and repetition behavior (Table 9, p. 15), monthly counts by user category (Table 10), full vs sampled word counts (Table 11), top words and 4-grams per month (Tables 12-25, pp. 16-18), common words across user categories (Table 26, p. 18), monthly prompts above and below 0.8 similarity (Tables 28-29), topic lists per month (Appendix D.1), CLIP semantic-clustering methods and counts across user categories (Appendix D.3, p. 27; Figures 13-15), and weighted and unweighted regressions of image similarity on token similarity and the number of identical tokens (Appendix E.1, p. 27).

paper_design_summary: The authors analyze Civiverse text-to-image prompts and generated images posted to CivitAI from October 2023 to April 2024; Section 3 reports 52,905 contributors to the original corpus and a subset of 2,747,380 unique prompts (p. 3). They track lexical diversity, near-duplicate prompt shares, and semantic diversity over time and across researcher-defined user groups based on observed repetition histories, and relate prompt diversity to visual diversity of the generated images. No person is assigned to a condition and no unassisted image-production group is observed.

participants.who: Corpus: Section 3 reports over 6.5 million images created by 52,905 unique contributors on CivitAI, October 2023 to April 2024; this is the reported corpus contributor count, not a verified post-exclusion people count for every sampled analysis. Section 3 reports exclusion of non-English prompts (3 percent), removal of 8,000 identical images with matching timestamps, and subsets of 5,864,047 prompts with duplicates and 2,747,380 unique prompts; subsequent analyses use the unique-prompt subset. Table 2 reports 25,058 consistent repeaters, 20,756 non-repeaters, and 7,091 occasional repeaters (p. 4). Appendix B, Table 9 instead reports 25,449 consistent repeaters, 7,093 occasional repeaters, and 21,835 non-repeaters (p. 15); the paper does not reconcile these counts. n_analyzed remains null because a single analysis-specific people count is not confirmed.
participants.quote: The Civiverse dataset [38] consists of over 6.5 million images created by a database of 52,905 unique contributors from the CivitAI platform
participants.locator: p. 3, Section 3; p. 4, Table 2; pp. 14-15, Appendix B and Table 9

ai_tool.name_model: Stable Diffusion family models and derivatives shared on CivitAI (the paper names Pony Diffusion XL, Stable Diffusion XL, Stable Diffusion 1.5, and Animagine XL v3.1)
ai_tool.how_used: Users write text prompts and the text-to-image model generates images; prompts and images are posted to the platform.

task.description: Writing text-to-image prompts and generating images on CivitAI in ordinary platform use

outcomes.name: Lexical diversity of prompts over time (TTR, ENW, SRS, CR)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Type-token ratio, effective number of words, self-repetition score over 4-grams, and gzip compression ratio, computed on each month's pool of prompts, in the full data and in a fixed-size sample of 213,779 prompts per month (Figure 3).

contrasts.reported: "TTR for April 2024 is 0.017 in the full data but rises to 0.023 when analyzing the fixed-size monthly sample"; "ENW ... decreases from around 3,500-3,600 in early 2024 to below 2,000 by April"; SRS and CR correlation r = -0.55; SRS full vs sampled correlation 0.9956

diversity_detail.metric: TTR, ENW, SRS, CR (lexical diversity of the monthly prompt pool)
diversity_detail.computed_over: All unique prompts in a month (full data), or a fixed-size sample of 213,779 prompts per month
diversity_detail.uncertainty: None reported; monthly point values only
diversity_detail.notes: Section 5.2 (p. 5) prints April 2024 TTR as 0.017 for the full data and 0.023 for the sampled data, and states that ENW falls below 2,000 by April. Figure 3a-b (p. 6) disagrees with the text for the April full-data TTR and ENW. Exact plotted endpoint values are not printed; no numerical estimates from the unlabelled points are recorded. The retained numbers are explicitly the main-text claims.

outcomes.name: Lexical diversity of prompts by user category (controlled sample)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: TTR, ENW, CR, and SRS on an equal sample of 90,521 prompts per user category; an uncontrolled version using all prompts is also reported in the text.

contrasts.reported: Consistent Repeaters TTR 0.065, ENW 2909, CR 0.26, SRS 5.75; Occasional Repeaters 0.076, 3483, 0.29, 5.83; Non-Repeaters 0.10, 3719, 0.39, 4.43

diversity_detail.computed_over: Pool of 90,521 prompts per user category

outcomes.name: Share of near-duplicate prompts (MinHash Jaccard similarity of at least 0.8)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: MinHash-LSH Jaccard similarity on prompts truncated to 20 tokens; threshold 0.8 (at least 16 shared tokens).

contrasts.reported: Above 0.8: 1,670,103 prompts, 34,034 users; below 0.8: 829,897 prompts, 43,587 users; "about 1.67 million (66.8%) surpass the 0.8 similarity threshold"; "From October 2023 to January 2024, high-similarity prompts account for approximately 68-73% of submissions"; "rising from 72.27% to 77.03% and surpassing 83% by April"
contrasts.locator: p. 7, Table 5 and Section 5.4; p. 20, Tables 28-29

diversity_detail.metric: Share of prompts with a near-duplicate at Jaccard similarity of at least 0.8
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each prompt against all others via MinHash-LSH
diversity_detail.notes: n_units is the "approximately 2.5 million sampled prompts" in Table 5. The monthly percentages in the p. 7 text (72.27, 77.03, above 83) match the consistent-repeater share column of Table 28, not the share of prompts above 0.8; Appendix C.6 (p. 19) describes 68.40 to 83.89 as the consistent-repeater share.

outcomes.name: Semantic diversity of prompts over time and across user categories (topic modeling and CLIP clustering)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Prompt specifiers embedded with MiniLM-L6-v2, reduced with UMAP, clustered with HDBSCAN; topics labelled with c-TF-IDF and GPT-4o. Section 6.3 describes a balanced subset of 90,521 unique prompts but does not explicitly state that this number is per user category. Non-repeaters have 89 topics, consistent repeaters 71, and occasional repeaters 76 (p. 9, Section 6.3). Appendix D.3 (p. 27) adds a semantic-diversity variant using whole-prompt CLIP clip-vit-base-p32 embeddings, clustered at cosine similarity >= 0.8 with a minimum cluster size of 20. It initially uses equal numbers of unique prompts per user category but does not state that initial number.

contrasts.reported: "the number of distinct semantic topics grew only modestly-rising from 72 in October to 83 in December and 89 by February-and even declined in March 2024"; "the topics-to-prompts ratio steadily decreased over time" (Figure 4c)

Consistent repeaters: 36,450 clustered prompts in 79 groups, including a cluster of 15,192 prompts; occasional repeaters: 31,223 clustered prompts in 166 groups; non-repeaters: 22,802 clustered prompts in 237 groups. The authors describe non-repeaters as having the greatest semantic diversity. These are prompt and cluster counts, not people counts; the initial sample size per category is not stated.
contrasts.locator: p. 27, Appendix D.3, methods and final paragraph; Figures 13-15

diversity_detail.metric: Monthly HDBSCAN topic count and topics-to-prompts ratio; topic counts across user categories; CLIP semantic-cluster counts and sizes across user categories (Appendix D.3)
diversity_detail.embedding_model: MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-dimensional); CLIP clip-vit-base-p32 for the Appendix D.3 variant
diversity_detail.computed_over: Prompt specifiers in each month and across user categories (Sections 6.1-6.3); whole-prompt CLIP embeddings from user-category samples in Appendix D.3. The initial D.3 samples have equal numbers of prompts, but that number is not stated.
diversity_detail.notes: Appendix D.1 lists 71 topics for October 2023, 73 for December 2023, 81 for February 2024, 76 for March 2024, and 83 for April 2024 (pp. 21-25), which differ from the p. 8 text. The raw topic count increases overall while the topics-to-prompts ratio decreases, so the temporal contrast is mixed. The Appendix D.3 counts are clustered prompts and clusters, not people; neither an initial per-category sample size nor an analysis-specific people count is stated there. n_units remains null.

outcomes.name: Visual diversity of generated images (Vendi score) over time and its link to prompt diversity
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Vendi score on samples of 10,000 prompts and images per user category per month (30,000 per month); the image representation behind the Vendi kernel is not stated. Pearson correlations of monthly lexical metrics with Vendi scores (Table 7). Cluster-level analysis relates token or CLIP text similarity to mean pairwise image-embedding cosine similarity (Figure 8, Appendix E.1).

contrasts.reported: Figure 6 only for levels; "a marked decline in Vendi scores is observed after February 2024". Table 7 correlations with Vendi: TTR 0.184 (p 0.349), ENW 0.521 (p 0.005), SRS -0.536 (p 0.003), CR 0.620 (p 0.012)
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Section 7.1 and Figure 6; p. 10, Table 7

diversity_detail.metric: Vendi score (effective number of distinct images)
diversity_detail.embedding_model: not stated for Vendi; CLIP clip-vit-base-p32 for the text embeddings in Section 7.2
diversity_detail.computed_over: Monthly samples of 10,000 images per user category
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Pearson correlation p-values only; no interval for Vendi levels
diversity_detail.notes: Section 7.2 (p. 10) reports token-image r = 0.33 with R² = 0.182 and text-image r = 0.43 with R² = 0.109. Figure 8a (p. 11) labels its x-axis Number of Identical Tokens and prints R² = 0.109; Figure 8b labels its x-axis Mean Text Embedding Similarity and prints R² = 0.182. Appendix E.1 (p. 27) separately labels its R² = 0.1821 analysis Token Similarity and its R² = 0.109 analysis Number of Identical Tokens. Figure 8b concerns semantic text-embedding similarity and does not print 0.1821. The differing labels, precision, and main-text/figure assignments are preserved without attempting to reconcile them.

eligibility.reason: Observational corpus study of existing CivitAI prompts and AI-generated images from October 2023 to April 2024, with no random assignment of people to AI assistance (pp. 3-4, Sections 3-4). Diversity is scored on prompts and images and compared across months and researcher-defined groups based on observed prompt-repetition histories (pp. 4-11, Sections 4-7; p. 27, Appendix D.3). The reported 52,905 contributors describe the original corpus; conflicting category counts and unspecified people counts for sampled analyses prevent confirmation of a single analysis-specific people count (p. 3, Section 3; p. 4, Table 2; p. 15, Table 9; pp. 9 and 27). The study qualifies as observational context and fails the random-assignment criterion for the core.

one_line_finding: In 2,747,380 unique CivitAI text-to-image prompts from October 2023 to April 2024, prompt lexical diversity fell (April 2024 TTR 0.017 full data, ENW below 2,000; p. 5), 66.8 percent of about 2.5 million prompts were near-duplicates at Jaccard 0.8 (Table 5, p. 7), image Vendi scores declined after February 2024 (Figure 6, p. 9), and monthly lexical diversity correlated with Vendi scores (CR rho = 0.620, SRS rho = -0.536; Table 7, p. 10).
notes: Several printed numbers disagree within the paper: April TTR and ENW in the p. 5 text vs Figure 3; monthly topic counts in the p. 8 text vs Appendix D.1; near-duplicate shares in the p. 7 text vs Table 28; R2 values and predictor labels in the p. 10 text vs Figure 8 and Appendix E.1; and user-category counts in Table 2 (p. 4) vs Table 9 (p. 15). Reported values are retained as printed, with the conflicts noted in the relevant diversity_detail.notes or participants.who field; no exact values are estimated from unlabelled plotted points.
